title: Local Dephasing Sustains Continuous Time Crystals in a Spin-1/2 Ensemble
abstract: Local pure dephasing suppresses single-spin coherence, yet we show that it sustains continuous time-crystalline order in a fully connected ferromagnetic spin-$1/2$ ensemble with local decay. An exact operator identity reveals the mechanism: dephasing raises the interaction energy, while energy relaxation on a finite timescale converts this charging into delayed feedback. Within homogeneous mean-field theory, we prove that dephasing is necessary for periodic motion in this model and that feedback exactly balances transverse damping over each cycle. Beyond mean field, the identity fixes the relative amplitude and phase of energy and longitudinal magnetization in oscillatory Liouvillian modes. Liouvillian spectra and stationary two-time correlations characterize temporal order through decay rates that decrease algebraically with system size, frequencies approaching nonzero mean-field values, and comparable per-spin oscillatory weights. Semiclassical trajectories further reveal recurrent switching between a limit-cycle region and two symmetry-related stationary regions: fluctuations interrupt and reactivate collective oscillations, and oscillatory episodes provide an intermediate channel between stationary regions. These results establish local dephasing as a resource for autonomous collective motion and show how the resulting temporal order can participate in metastable dynamics.
summary: This work demonstrates that local pure dephasing can sustain continuous time-crystalline order in a ferromagnetic spin ensemble. The mechanism relies on an exact energy identity showing that dephasing-induced energy relaxation creates a delayed feedback loop that balances damping. This establishes dephasing as a key resource for autonomous collective quantum motion.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether local pure dephasing can sustain continuous time-crystalline order in a quantum spin ensemble, contrasting this with mechanisms relying on population changes.
main_result: Local dephasing is shown to be necessary for persistent collective oscillations, as the resulting energy relaxation provides a delayed feedback mechanism that exactly compensates for transverse damping.
method: The analysis uses mean-field theory, deriving Bloch equations and employing exact operator identities to analyze energy conservation and feedback mechanisms.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous ensemble of spin-1/2 particles with all-to-all ferromagnetic interactions, governed by a master equation incorporating both decay ($\gamma$) and pure dephasing ($\gamma_\phi$).
key_observables: Magnetization components ($m_x, m_y, m_z$), Liouvillian spectra, stationary two-time correlations, and power spectra $S_{zz}(\omega)$.
important_parameters: The ratio of dephasing to decay ($\gamma_\phi/\gamma$), interaction strength ($J$), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially relies on the homogeneous mean-field approximation, though it extends to quantum signatures and semiclassical trajectories.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate dephasing-controlled oscillations, response maps in the interaction–dephasing plane showing P/C regimes, and diagrams detailing the delayed energy feedback loop in the mean-field dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model and mean-field equations, proving the necessity of dephasing for periodicity via energy identities, analyzing the delayed feedback mechanism, and finally examining quantum signatures and robustness against parameter noise.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical mechanism showing how purely dissipative processes (dephasing) can act as a resource to maintain non-equilibrium, periodic collective motion in quantum many-body systems.
